title: Mocking an accent
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in the Emergency Department. At the nurses' station, two nurses are imitating the accent of Mrs Nowak, a Polish patient they have just seen, and laughing.

Several patients in nearby cubicles, including Mrs Nowak, may be able to hear them.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Suggest respect for patients as a topic for the next team teaching.
options.brief: Useful, but it does nothing about what's happening now.
options.detailed: Teaching can help change culture over time, but it doesn't address this incident.

options.text: Mention it to the nurse in charge after your shift.
options.brief: Helps address the behaviour more widely.
options.detailed: The nurse in charge can address it with the staff involved. It ranks third because it is less immediate.

options.text: Check that Mrs Nowak is all right, and apologise if she heard.
options.brief: She may have been hurt by what she heard.
options.detailed: If she heard, an apology on behalf of the department helps restore her trust. It ranks second because stopping the behaviour comes first.

options.text: Ask them calmly to stop, as patients can hear them.
options.brief: Stops the behaviour straight away without a confrontation.
options.detailed: A calm, brief request deals with it at once. Pointing out that patients can hear gives a clear, non-accusatory reason. It ranks first.

options.text: Leave it, as it's only a joke between colleagues.
options.brief: Discriminatory behaviour that patients can hear isn't harmless.
options.detailed: Mocking a patient's accent is disrespectful and could be discriminatory. Doing nothing allows it to continue. It is the least appropriate option.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you challenge discriminatory behaviour by colleagues, especially when patients may be affected.
explanation.keyDetails: The nurses are mocking a patient's accent. Patients can hear. It is happening now.
explanation.reasoning: [D] stops it, [C] supports the patient, and [B] addresses it further. [A] is too distant, and [E] allows it to continue.
explanation.competing: [C] and [B] are close. The key puts Mrs Nowak first because she may have been directly hurt.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 2, treating patients fairly and with respect.

references.title: Equality Act 2010
references.note: Race and national origin as protected characteristics.
